summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 72 needed discussion before planning, clean up stale/drifted todos across Phases 70-73, then run the full plan→execute→ship flow for Phase 72 (with Phase 73 to follow) — interrupted midway by CI regressions and flakiness that had to be fixed first.
summary.outcome: Fixed and merged two CI regression PRs (#601 FUSE seq-equivocation, #600 web floor helper + sdk-e2e Test 21 + web-e2e flake stabilization), then completed Phase 72 planning and executed all 10 plans across 7 waves (SC#1-SC#6 all landed, final integration gate green), with a newly-scoped follow-up task (test-file TS drift + CI typecheck gate) left in progress at end of transcript.

repo: GSD retires todos by deleting/moving files between .planning/todos/pending/ and completed/ — Phase 71 shipped without doing this, leaving 8 stale todos in pending/ despite being addressed in shipped code.
ci-e2e.yml (Web/Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PR authors must manually dispatch against their branch to get real e2e signal pre-merge.
gh workflow run -f ref=<branch> returns HTTP 422 'Unexpected inputs' on this repo's workflow definitions; use `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` instead.

Playwright web-e2e's ciFloor() helper only raises wait timeouts to 60s under CI (process.env.CI) — local runs use much tighter timeouts (15-30s), causing IPNS-gated-mutation tests to flake locally even though they pass reliably in CI.

playwright.config.ts webServer uses reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI, so setting CI=1 locally to match CI's timeout floor conflicts with an already-running dev stack (must patch config or restart stack).

Root `pnpm typecheck` only runs each package's build (tsconfig.build.json, tests excluded) — test files are never typechecked in CI, allowing vitest-v2→v3 Mock-generic drift and Phase-62 type-retirement fallout to accumulate silently in test files.

@cipherbox/* workspace packages resolve types via built `dist` (no path aliases or TS project references), so a 'typecheck before build' CI gate must interleave per-package in dependency order (tc→build→tc→build...), not run as one upfront pass.

IPNS anti-equivocation gate (Phase 71, ipns.service.ts) rejects same-sequence republish with a different CID — FUSE's publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish (gated on 'inode cid empty'), so a dropped/stale re-publish with a fresh CID legitimately triggered the gate.
Fresh git worktrees fail for this pnpm monorepo because node_modules isn't present — sequential execution on the main tree is the reliable choice for phase execution.
Committing on this repo can hang/false-negative due to a 1Password SSH-signing prompt; always verify with `git log`/`git status` whether the commit actually landed before retrying.

code.finding: publish_file_node's first-publish branch hardcoded seq=1 without resolving first; fixed to resolve via resolve_ipns_for_replay and fall through to publish_with_cas_retry (with a captured resolved_seq) when the name is already Found, avoiding equivocation.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param so callers that already resolved the sequence (e.g. content_ops.rs Found path) skip a redundant second resolve round-trip; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after conflict.

ciFloor() helper raises waitForItemToDisappear and similar waits to a 60s floor only under CI — local callers keep whatever literal timeout they specify, which is the root cause of local-only flakiness on IPNS-gated mutation tests.

6.6.2's post-restore gate (getVersionCount()===1) is a no-op since a restore swap keeps the count at 1 both before and after — replaced with expect.poll() re-reading actual editor content until it matches, since the text editor always re-fetches fresh from the API with no in-memory cache to invalidate.

workflow: When a CI e2e workflow doesn't run on PRs, dispatch it manually via workflow_dispatch against the fix branch for real pre-merge validation instead of merging blind and trusting the post-merge main run.

When a subagent's root-cause fix works but a downstream step still fails, check whether the failure moved further into the flow (e.g., FUSE equivocation gone but a stale test-driver DTO field now surfaces a different 400) rather than assuming the fix failed.

For diagnosing intermittent local flakes that pass in CI, running the test locally under CI's exact timeout regime (CI=1, matching workers/retries) is more representative than iterating with local defaults, even though it requires reconciling config side-effects like webServer.reuseExistingServer.

When a background CI/local run repeatedly fails at a different, earlier point each retry (ambient stack degradation), it's a signal to switch to a representative harness (e.g., CI-equivalent timeout regime) rather than continuing to bump individual timeouts test-by-test.

Raw JSON extracted via CLI tools (e.g., hook definitions with multiline string values) may not parse with standard JSON.parse — a custom lenient parser that escapes control chars only inside string literals was needed.

friction: Initially checked the wrong todo directory (resolved/ instead of completed/), requiring user correction mid-turn.
gh workflow run -f ref=<branch> failed with HTTP 422 because the workflow definition on main predates that input; had to switch to --ref.

Reproducing web-e2e flakes locally required 7 separate local/CI-regime runs across multiple different tests (4.10, 4.11, 2.1) that each blocked the serial test chain from reaching the actual target fixes (6.6.2, 8.2) due to local timeouts being tighter than CI's ciFloor-adjusted ones.
CI=1 locally conflicted with playwright's reuseExistingServer config, requiring a temporary (later reverted) patch to playwright.config.ts to validate under CI's real timeout regime.
lint-staged commit appeared to time out at 2 minutes (likely a 1Password SSH-signing prompt hang), requiring manual verification that the commit had actually landed.
git cat-file checks initially gave conflicting/incorrect results about whether the todo completed/ files were in HEAD, requiring a second decisive check to resolve.
Raw hook JSON (plan:pre fragments) contained literal control characters that broke standard JSON parsing, requiring a custom script to extract research/pattern-mapper/tdd/schema-gate fragments.

The gsd-executor sandbox couldn't access .env, so several live sdk-e2e tests (bin-operations, resurrection-guard confirmation) were implemented and typechecked but not actually run during execution — deferred to phase verification.

Full inventory of test-file TS drift (113 errors across 15 files) turned out broader than the initial vitest-v2→v3 Mock-typing hypothesis — sdk package errors were actually Phase-62 type-retirement fallout (stale imports/fixtures), requiring a more careful, non-mechanical migration.
